title: Player — beta usage (server-side truth)
description:
Server-side counterpart to the Umami views (#2268, epic #2263). Umami answers what people DID in the browser; these four panels answer what the SERVER saw, which is the only view that survives a browser-side analytics failure — an ad blocker, a CSP, a tracker that never loaded. The two disagreeing is itself the signal.

Every panel filters on $instance. The existing dashboards in this repo hardcode `instance:prod-podcast`; this one does not, because the same four questions have to be answerable against a dev deploy while a change is being proven, and a dashboard that can only read prod gets validated by being stared at.

Panel 4 is not a vanity panel. The three player log streams read ZERO on prod right now: the Alloy `local.file_match` glob pointed at `corpus/users/*/listen.jsonl` while the server writes `player-appdata/users/<id>/listen_events.jsonl` — wrong directory AND wrong filename. Nothing errored. The panels simply read empty, and empty reads as 'nobody used it'. Panel 4 exists so that failure can never again be mistaken for a quiet week.

list.name: instance
list.label: Deploy
list.description: The deploy's `instance` label. Prod ships as `prod-podcast` (cluster `vps`); a local validation run seeds `dev-local` (cluster `local`). A custom list rather than a label-values query so the dashboard still offers both when one of them has no rows at all — which is exactly the state panel 4 exists to make visible.

panels.title: Signups per day (server-side)
panels.description: From `account_events.jsonl` (`append_account_created`), so it counts a signup even when the browser's analytics never loaded. It is also what anchors the 24-hour window for 'Activated': a signup Umami missed still has a start time to measure from.

targets.expr: instance:$instance AND job:podcast-accounts AND event_type:account_created | stats count() signups

panels.title: Playback depth — how far people actually get
panels.description:
The milestone ladder from `playback_events.jsonl`. Only 25/50/75/95 are recorded (`PLAYBACK_MILESTONES`), and the route plus a second guard in `append_playback_progress` both reject anything else, so a bar outside those four means something is writing events this app does not emit.

Read it as a funnel, not four independent numbers: the drop between 25 and 95 is the single most honest measure of whether episodes hold people. A ladder that does NOT thin as it deepens is a bug, not a triumph.

targets.expr: instance:$instance AND job:podcast-playback AND event_type:playback_progress | stats by (milestone) count() reached

panels.title: Episodes started per day (server-side)
panels.description: From `listen_events.jsonl` (`append_listen_event`, ADR-119 envelope, `event_type: listen`). Compare against Umami's `play_start`: the server count is the floor, because it cannot be blocked by the listener's browser. A persistent gap between the two is a measurement of how much browser-side analytics is being lost, which is worth knowing on its own.

targets.expr: instance:$instance AND job:podcast-listen AND event_type:listen | stats count() listens

panels.title: Shipper health — rows per player log stream (0 = BROKEN, not quiet)
panels.description:
THE PANEL THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE ORIGINAL BUG.

All three player streams read zero on prod at the time of writing, and nothing anywhere said so. The Alloy `local.file_match` glob watched `corpus/users/*/listen.jsonl`; the server writes `player-appdata/users/<id>/listen_events.jsonl`. Wrong directory and wrong filename. The shipper itself was fine — the identical block one line above it delivered `podcast-search` (328 rows) and `podcast-jobs` (1208 rows) — so there was no error to find, only three panels quietly reading empty.

An empty analytics panel is ambiguous in the worst possible direction: it looks exactly like a product nobody used. This panel removes the ambiguity. A missing row here means the PIPELINE is broken; a zero in panels 1–3 with rows here means the product genuinely was not used.

The thresholds colour zero red deliberately. If a stream is absent from this table entirely, that is worse than a zero, because the glob is matching no file at all.

targets.expr: instance:$instance AND job:~"podcast-(listen|playback|accounts)" | stats by (job) count() rows
